pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: This Old Man
work.note: Ponte cultural: This Old Man. This Old Man é uma cantiga tradicional britânica de contar, registrada por escrito no início do século XX. Em cada estrofe, um velhinho toca um som diferente em uma parte do corpo, e a cada número a letra muda. Por isso a música serve para ensinar a contar de um a dez e é muito usada com crianças pequenas. A aula retorna à obra para explorar “os números de 6 a 10 e a dizer valores em dól

pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

facts.label: Situação
facts.sub: In New York City, you can buy pizza by the slice and eat it on the street in two minutes. Learn how to order, pay and eat it like a New Yorker.

facts.big: In New York, many pizza shops sell single slices.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: You can order one, two or more slices and eat right away.

facts.big: People often fold a New York slice before they eat it.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: The slice is large and thin, so folding it is easy and clean.

facts.big: Pepperoni is a very common topping in the USA.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: Pepperoni is one of the most popular pizza toppings in the USA.

facts.label: Educação e tom
facts.sub: Say Can I get…? or Two slices, please, then Thanks! Keep it short; the line is moving.

compare.br: In Brazil, pizza is often a whole pie shared by a group, at a pizzeria or delivery, with a knife and fork or by hand.
compare.us: In New York, a quick slice is a street meal: you stand, eat with your hands and pay a few dollars.
compare.tip: Know your numbers: three dollars is “three dollars”, not “three”.
compare.ask: How do you eat pizza? With your hands or knife and fork? Say it in English.

pages.title: My first slice in New York · 1/3
paragraphs: Today I am in **New York**, and I am very hungry. On the corner, I see a pizza shop with a big sign: “Pizza by the slice.” I go in.

A man called Ravi says, “Hi! **What can I get you?**” I say, “**Two slices of pepperoni, please.**” He puts the slices in a hot oven, and in a minute they are ready. “**Anything to drink?**” he asks. “A soda, please.” “**Small or large?**” “Large. **How much is it?**” “**That’s eight dollars.**” I say, “**Here you go. Thanks!**” and he says, “**Enjoy your pizza!**”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: My first slice in New York · 2/3
paragraphs: The slices are huge! A woman next to me **folds** her slice in half and eats it with her hands. I do the same. It is hot, cheesy and so good. A man says, “**New York style, baby!**”

I remember a song from my English class, “This Old Man”. It is a British counting song, written down in the early 1900s. It counts from one to ten, and each number has a rhyme. I count my dollars too: one, two, three… up to ten.

pages.title: My first slice in New York · 3/3
paragraphs: I give Ravi ten dollars, and he gives me two dollars back. “**Keep the change**,” I say, and I smile. It is a great lunch, and it costs only a few dollars.

pages.title: Palavras pelo contexto

items.q: The slice is huge! O que significa “huge”?
items.why: Huge = very big.

items.q: She folds her slice in half. O que significa “folds”?
items.why: Fold = bend over itself.

items.q: Keep the change, please. O que significa “change”?
items.why: Change = the money returned to you.

pages.instruction: Use a frase inteira como pista.

pages.title: Confira as pistas

items.q: The pizza shop sells whole pizzas only.
items.why: The sign says “Pizza by the slice.”

items.q: The writer orders a large soda.
items.why: “Large. How much is it?”

items.q: The writer pays nine dollars.
items.why: The price is eight dollars; the writer gives ten.

items.q: The writer eats with hands.
items.why: The writer folds the slice and eats it.
